evals.name: missing-package-after-creation
evals.prompt: I'm in a repo whose flake.nix outputs are `inputs: inputs.blueprint { inherit inputs; prefix = "nix"; }`. I just created nix/packages/mytool/default.nix and nix/packages/mytool/package.nix, but `nix build .#mytool` says the attribute 'mytool' is missing and `nix flake show` doesn't list it. The nix files evaluate fine when I import them manually. What's wrong?
evals.trap: The evaluation-looks-fine detail tempts a deep dive into the nix expressions; the actual cause is that untracked files are invisible to flake evaluation

assertions.text: Identifies untracked files as the primary suspect and asks for or runs git status
States that git add (staging) is sufficient, no commit needed
Does not propose editing flake.nix to register the package (blueprint has no registration step)
Mentions meta.platforms filtering or name shadowing only as secondary checks, if at all

evals.name: add-package-two-file-pattern
evals.prompt: This repo uses blueprint with prefix = "nix" and already has nix/devshell.nix and nix/formatter.nix. Add a Nix package for the Go CLI that lives in this repo (standard go.mod at the repo root), so `nix build .#mycli` works.
evals.trap: Tempts writing a single default.nix that declares { buildGoModule, lib }: directly, which fails because blueprint's callPackage scope only has inputs/flake/pkgs/system/perSystem/pname

assertions.text: Creates nix/packages/mycli/ (directory with default.nix, or a single mycli.nix) — not an entry in flake.nix
The file loaded by blueprint only requests arguments from the blueprint scope (pkgs, flake, perSystem, inputs, system, pname)
If a nixpkgs-style package.nix is written, it is bridged via pkgs.callPackage ./package.nix { ... } from the default.nix shim
Uses the flake (or a path within it) as src, e.g. src = flake
Reminds to git add the new files or verifies visibility with nix flake show / nix eval

evals.name: wrong-scope-argument-error
evals.prompt: In a blueprint repo, nix build fails with: error: evaluation aborted with the following error message: 'lib.customisation.callPackageWith: Function called without required argument "stdenv" at /nix/store/...-source/nix/packages/tool.nix:1'. The file starts with `{ stdenv, lib }:`. Fix it.
evals.trap: Tempts adding stdenv to some configuration or overlay; the fix is understanding the fixed per-system scope

assertions.text: Explains that blueprint files receive only inputs/flake/pkgs/system/perSystem/pname, not arbitrary nixpkgs attributes
Fixes by taking pkgs and using pkgs.stdenv/pkgs.lib, or by moving the nixpkgs-style code to a package.nix loaded via pkgs.callPackage
Does not suggest overlays or modifying flake.nix to inject stdenv

evals.name: formatter-check-never-runs
evals.prompt: Our blueprint repo has a treefmt-based nix/formatter.nix that ends with: formatter // { meta = formatter.meta // { tests = { check = check; }; }; }. CI runs `nix flake check` and it's green, but I broke formatting on purpose and it stayed green. checks.x86_64-linux shows pkgs-formatter but no pkgs-formatter-check. Why doesn't the check run?
evals.trap: Everything looks wired up; the bug is meta.tests vs passthru.tests — blueprint only collects passthru.tests into checks

assertions.text: Identifies that blueprint collects passthru.tests, and meta.tests is silently ignored
Rewrites the tail to formatter // { passthru = formatter.passthru // { tests.check = check; }; } or equivalent
Verifies with nix eval .#checks.<system> --apply builtins.attrNames that pkgs-formatter-check now appears

evals.name: add-nixos-host-with-input-modules
evals.prompt: This blueprint repo (no prefix) already has hosts/sirius/configuration.nix and modules/nixos/{core,networking}.nix. Add a new host 'orion' (x86_64-linux) that needs the disko module from inputs.disko and should reuse the existing shared nixos modules.
evals.trap: configuration.nix alone gives no place to import inputs.disko.nixosModules.disko into the module list; the established pattern is the hosts/<name>/default.nix escape hatch returning { class, value }

assertions.text: Creates files under hosts/orion/ rather than editing flake.nix

Either uses hosts/orion/default.nix returning { class = "nixos"; value = nixosSystem { ... }; } to inject disko's module, or imports the disko module from within configuration.nix via inputs — and wires specialArgs (flake/inputs/hostName) if hand-rolling nixosSystem
Reuses shared modules via flake.modules.nixos.* (or inputs.self.nixosModules)
Sets nixpkgs.hostPlatform (or system) for the host
Knows the output will appear as nixosConfigurations.orion and can be checked with nix eval .#nixosConfigurations --apply builtins.attrNames

evals.name: flake-show-broken-by-wip-host
evals.prompt: After I created an empty directory hosts/newbox/ (I planned to fill it in later, it only has a .gitkeep) in our blueprint repo, `nix flake show` now fails with: error: host 'newbox' does not have a configuration. Other outputs won't evaluate either. What are my options?
evals.trap: Tempts blaming the newest configuration.nix or nix version; the rule is that every hosts/<name>/ directory must contain a recognized configuration file or home users, otherwise evaluation of host outputs throws

assertions.text: Explains that hosts/<name>/ must contain default.nix, configuration.nix, darwin-configuration.nix, system-configuration.nix, rpi-configuration.nix, or users/ home configs
Offers removing the directory or adding a minimal recognized file as the fix
Notes the throw breaks host-derived outputs globally, which is why unrelated outputs failed

evals.name: new-project-setup
evals.prompt: Set up a new Nix flake for a Python project using numtide/blueprint. I want the nix files under a nix/ directory, a default devshell with python313 and uv, and a treefmt formatter. Nothing else yet.
evals.trap: Tempts writing devShells/formatter outputs by hand in flake.nix, or forgetting prefix must match the directory, or forgetting git add before the first nix develop

assertions.text: flake.nix outputs are just inputs.blueprint { inherit inputs; prefix = "nix"; } with nixpkgs+blueprint (and treefmt-nix) inputs — no hand-written devShells/formatter attributes
Creates nix/devshell.nix taking { pkgs } or { pkgs, perSystem } and evaluating to a mkShell derivation
Creates nix/formatter.nix (e.g. treefmt-nix mkWrapper) rather than a formatter output in flake.nix
Runs or instructs git init/git add before testing with nix develop / nix flake show

evals.name: shadowed-directory-edit-does-nothing
evals.prompt: In our blueprint repo, editing nix/packages/agent/default.nix does nothing — nix build .#agent keeps producing the old derivation, even after git add -A and with no eval cache. There is also a file nix/packages/agent.nix from an old refactor. Why are my edits ignored?
evals.trap: The stale-cache red herring; the real cause is that agent.nix shadows the agent/ directory in blueprint's importDir (nix files take precedence over directories of the same name)

assertions.text: Identifies that packages/agent.nix takes precedence over packages/agent/ and the directory is silently ignored
Fix: delete or rename one of the two (keep a single source)
Does not send the user chasing nix caches or store garbage collection
